nodes.statement_short: On the support $\norm[x]_{\F}^{\sigma} \leq q^{-\sigma D(\Phi)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.24
nodes.statement: The first follows from $$ B_l^{\sigma}(f)^l \leq B_{\infty}^{\sigma-\epsilon}(f) \sum_{n \geq 0} q^{-n\epsilon} + B_{\infty}^{\sigma+\epsilon}(f) \sum_{n < 0} q^{n\epsilon}. $$ The second is obvious by positivity.
nodes.statement_short: Geometric summation over $n \geq 0$ and $n<0$ for the first inequality; positivity of terms for the second.

nodes.name: Geometric summation
nodes.statement: The first follows from $$ B_l^{\sigma}(f)^l \leq B_{\infty}^{\sigma-\epsilon}(f) \sum_{n \geq 0} q^{-n\epsilon} + B_{\infty}^{\sigma+\epsilon}(f) \sum_{n < 0} q^{n\epsilon}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Split the sum at $n=0$ and sum two geometric series.

nodes.name: Reverse inequality by positivity
nodes.statement: The second is obvious by positivity.
nodes.statement_short: Each term is dominated by the full sum.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.25
nodes.statement: The first is obvious. For the second, let $s_0$ be any complex number with $\Re s_0 = \sigma$ and $0 < \Im s_0 < 2\pi / \log q$. Selecting the contour joining $\sigma+\epsilon$, $\sigma+\epsilon + i 2\pi / \log q$, $\sigma - \epsilon + i 2\pi / \log q$ and $\sigma-\epsilon$, we see $$ \log q \cdot M(s_0) = \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{M(\sigma+\epsilon+i\tau)}{\sigma+\epsilon+i\tau - s_0} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} - \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{M(\sigma-\epsilon+i\tau)}{\sigma-\epsilon+i\tau - s_0} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi}. $$ Using H\"older inequality we deduce \begin{align*} \log q \cdot \norm[M(s_0)] &\leq \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma+\epsilon}(M) \cdot \left( \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} \right)^{\frac{l-1}{l}} + \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma-\epsilon}(M) \cdot \left( \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} \right)^{\frac{l-1}{l}} \\ &= \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma+\epsilon}(M) + \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma-\epsilon}(M). \end{align*} We conclude by taking $\sup$ with respect to $\Re s_0 = \sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: Represent $M(s_0)$ by a rectangular contour of vertical width $2\pi/\log q$ and apply Holder on the two vertical sides.

nodes.name: First inequality is trivial
nodes.statement: The first is obvious.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the definitions.

nodes.name: Contour representation of $M(s_0)$
nodes.statement: For the second, let $s_0$ be any complex number with $\Re s_0 = \sigma$ and $0 < \Im s_0 < 2\pi / \log q$. Selecting the contour joining $\sigma+\epsilon$, $\sigma+\epsilon + i 2\pi / \log q$, $\sigma - \epsilon + i 2\pi / \log q$ and $\sigma-\epsilon$, we see $$ \log q \cdot M(s_0) = \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{M(\sigma+\epsilon+i\tau)}{\sigma+\epsilon+i\tau - s_0} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} - \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{M(\sigma-\epsilon+i\tau)}{\sigma-\epsilon+i\tau - s_0} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi}. $$

nodes.name: Bound by Holder and take the supremum
nodes.statement: Using H\"older inequality we deduce \begin{align*} \log q \cdot \norm[M(s_0)] &\leq \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma+\epsilon}(M) \cdot \left( \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} \right)^{\frac{l-1}{l}} + \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma-\epsilon}(M) \cdot \left( \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} \right)^{\frac{l-1}{l}} \\ &= \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma+\epsilon}(M) + \frac{1}{\epsilon} H_l^{\sigma-\epsilon}(M). \end{align*} We conclude by taking $\sup$ with respect to $\Re s_0 = \sigma$.
nodes.statement_short: Holder on both vertical sides gives $\epsilon^{-1}(H_l^{\sigma+\epsilon}+H_l^{\sigma-\epsilon})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.26
nodes.statement: The continuity follows from $$ H_{\infty}^{\sigma}(\Mellin{f}) \leq \sum_{n \in \ag{Z}} \norm[f(\varpi^n)] q^{-n\sigma} = B_1^{\sigma}(f); $$ $$ B_{\infty}^{\sigma}(f_M) \leq \sup_{n \in \ag{Z}} \int_0^{\frac{2\pi}{\log q}} \norm[M(\sigma+i\tau) q^{n i \tau}] \frac{\log q d\tau}{2\pi} = H_1^{\sigma}(M). $$
nodes.statement_short: Term-by-term estimates give $H_{\infty}^{\sigma}(\Mellin{f}) \leq B_1^{\sigma}(f)$ and $B_{\infty}^{\sigma}(f_M) \leq H_1^{\sigma}(M)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.28

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.35
nodes.statement: We treat the case for $\Gamma_0(N)$. Take any $A \in \SL_r(\ag{Z})$. Let the first column of $A$ be $(a_1,\cdots,a_r)^T \in \ag{Z}^r$. Then we have $\lcd(a_1,\cdots,a_r)=1$, which implies the existence of $u_i \in \ag{Z}$ such that $\Sigma_{i=1}^r u_i a_i = 1$. In particular, we have $\lcd(u_1,a_2,\cdots,a_r)=1$. For any $k_j \in \ag{Z}, 2 \leq j \leq r$, the substitution $$ u_1' = u_1+\sum_{j=2}^r k_j a_j; u_j' = u_j-k_j, 2 \leq j \leq r $$ still gives $\Sigma_{i=1}^r u_i' a_i = 1$. By an iterative application of Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progression, we can choose $k_j$'s such that $u_1'$ is a prime number as large as we want. In particular, we can make $\lcd(u_1',N)=1$. Since $\lcd(u_1',\cdots,u_r')=1$, at least one of $u_j', 2 \leq j \leq r$, say $u_2'$, is coprime with $u_1'$. Hence $\lcd(u_1',Nu_2')=1$ and we can find $v_1,v_2 \in \ag{Z}$ such that $u_1'v_2-Nu_2'v_1=1$. The matrix $$ B = \begin{pmatrix} u_1' & u_2' & u_3' \cdots \\ Nv_1 & v_2 & 0 \cdots \\ \vec{0} & \vec{0} & I_{r-2} \end{pmatrix} \in \Gamma_0(N) $$ and gives, for some $A'=\tilde{A}-\vec{\alpha} \vec{\beta_1}^T \in \SL_{r-1}(\ag{Z})$, that $$ BA = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \vec{\beta_1}^T \\ \vec{\alpha} & \tilde{A} \end{pmatrix} \Rightarrow A \in \Gamma_0(N) \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \\ \vec{\alpha} & A' \end{pmatrix} n_r^+(\vec{\beta_1}). $$ Repeating the process on $A'$ or making an induction on $r$ we then find successively $\vec{\beta_k} \in \ag{Z}^{r-k}$ such that for some lower unipotent $N_-^1$ $$ A \in \Gamma_0(N) N_-^1 N_+^1, N_+^1=\prod_{k=0}^{r-2} \begin{pmatrix} I_k & 0 \\ 0 & n_{r-k}^+(\vec{\beta_{k+1}}) \end{pmatrix}. $$ Taking $N_-$ resp. $N_+$ with off-diagonal entries lying in $[-\frac{N}{2}, \frac{N}{2}] \cap \ag{Z}$ such that $N_-^1 \equiv N_- \pmod{N}$ resp. $N_+^1 \equiv N_+ \pmod{N}$, we then find $N_-^1 N_-^{-1}, N_+^1 N_+^{-1} \in \Gamma(N)$ and conclude by its normality.
nodes.statement_short: Use Dirichlet on primes in arithmetic progressions to make the first row coprime to $N$, build $B \in \Gamma_0(N)$ peeling off one unipotent factor, induct on $r$, then reduce the entries mod $N$ using normality of $\Gamma(N)$.

nodes.name: Start from a Bezout relation for the first column
nodes.statement: We treat the case for $\Gamma_0(N)$. Take any $A \in \SL_r(\ag{Z})$. Let the first column of $A$ be $(a_1,\cdots,a_r)^T \in \ag{Z}^r$. Then we have $\lcd(a_1,\cdots,a_r)=1$, which implies the existence of $u_i \in \ag{Z}$ such that $\Sigma_{i=1}^r u_i a_i = 1$. In particular, we have $\lcd(u_1,a_2,\cdots,a_r)=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $u_i$ with $\sum u_ia_i=1$.

nodes.name: Adjust by Dirichlet so that $u_1'$ is prime and coprime to $N$
nodes.statement: For any $k_j \in \ag{Z}, 2 \leq j \leq r$, the substitution $$ u_1' = u_1+\sum_{j=2}^r k_j a_j; u_j' = u_j-k_j, 2 \leq j \leq r $$ still gives $\Sigma_{i=1}^r u_i' a_i = 1$. By an iterative application of Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progression, we can choose $k_j$'s such that $u_1'$ is a prime number as large as we want. In particular, we can make $\lcd(u_1',N)=1$. Since $\lcd(u_1',\cdots,u_r')=1$, at least one of $u_j', 2 \leq j \leq r$, say $u_2'$, is coprime with $u_1'$. Hence $\lcd(u_1',Nu_2')=1$ and we can find $v_1,v_2 \in \ag{Z}$ such that $u_1'v_2-Nu_2'v_1=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Iterated Dirichlet on arithmetic progressions makes $u_1'$ a large prime coprime to $N$.

nodes.name: Build $B \in \Gamma_0(N)$ and peel off one unipotent factor
nodes.statement: $$ B = \begin{pmatrix} u_1' & u_2' & u_3' \cdots \\ Nv_1 & v_2 & 0 \cdots \\ \vec{0} & \vec{0} & I_{r-2} \end{pmatrix} \in \Gamma_0(N) $$ and gives, for some $A'=\tilde{A}-\vec{\alpha} \vec{\beta_1}^T \in \SL_{r-1}(\ag{Z})$, that $$ BA = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \vec{\beta_1}^T \\ \vec{\alpha} & \tilde{A} \end{pmatrix} \Rightarrow A \in \Gamma_0(N) \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \\ \vec{\alpha} & A' \end{pmatrix} n_r^+(\vec{\beta_1}). $$
nodes.statement_short: Left multiplication by $B$ normalizes the first row, exhibiting $A \in \Gamma_0(N) N_- A' n_r^+$.

nodes.name: Iterate / induct on the rank
nodes.statement: Repeating the process on $A'$ or making an induction on $r$ we then find successively $\vec{\beta_k} \in \ag{Z}^{r-k}$ such that for some lower unipotent $N_-^1$ $$ A \in \Gamma_0(N) N_-^1 N_+^1, N_+^1=\prod_{k=0}^{r-2} \begin{pmatrix} I_k & 0 \\ 0 & n_{r-k}^+(\vec{\beta_{k+1}}) \end{pmatrix}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Repeating on $A'$ produces $A \in \Gamma_0(N)N_-^1N_+^1$.

nodes.name: Reduce entries mod $N$ using normality of $\Gamma(N)$
nodes.statement: Taking $N_-$ resp. $N_+$ with off-diagonal entries lying in $[-\frac{N}{2}, \frac{N}{2}] \cap \ag{Z}$ such that $N_-^1 \equiv N_- \pmod{N}$ resp. $N_+^1 \equiv N_+ \pmod{N}$, we then find $N_-^1 N_-^{-1}, N_+^1 N_+^{-1} \in \Gamma(N)$ and conclude by its normality.
nodes.statement_short: Replace $N_{\pm}^1$ by representatives with entries in $[-N/2,N/2]$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.36
nodes.statement_short: Compare $f_c$ with the Euclidean norm, use the elementary divisor theorem plus Lemma 5.35 to bound the operator norm of the lattice basis, then a diameter/volume comparison for part (2).

nodes.name: Compare $f_c$ with the Euclidean norm
nodes.statement: (1) On $\ag{R}^{r_1} \times \ag{C}^{r_2}$ we have a usual norm $\Norm_2$ given by $$ \Norm[\vec{x}]_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{r_1+r_2} \norm[x_i]^2}, \vec{x}=(x_i)_{1 \leq i \leq r_1+r_2}. $$ We then easily see, essentially by comparing $f_c$ with the infinity norm, that $$ \sup_{\vec{x}} f_c(\vec{x}) \Norm[\vec{x}]_2^c \leq (r_1+r_2)^{\frac{c}{2}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: $\sup_{\vec{x}} f_c(\vec{x})\Norm[\vec{x}]_2^c \leq (r_1+r_2)^{c/2}$.

nodes.name: Introduce the lattice norm and the elementary divisor decomposition
nodes.statement:
If $\alpha_i \in \idlJ^{-1}$ is an integral basis such that $\idlJ^{-1}=\Sigma_{i=1}^r \ag{Z} \alpha_i$, then $\sigma(\alpha_i)$ is a basis of the lattice $\sigma(\idlJ^{-1})$. We can define another norm $\Norm_{\idlJ^{-1}}$ by $$ \Norm[\vec{x}]_{\idlJ^{-1}}=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^r n_i^2}, \vec{x} = \sum_{i=1}^r n_i \sigma(\alpha_i) \in \ag{R}^r. $$ Or equivalently, if we write $A_{\idlJ^{-1}}=(\sigma(\alpha_1), \cdots, \sigma(\alpha_r)) \in \GL_r(\ag{R})$, we have $$ \Norm[\vec{x}]_{\idlJ^{-1}} = \Norm[A_{\idlJ^{-1}}^{-1}\vec{x}]_2. $$ Fix a basis $\vec{e_i}$ of $\sigma(\vo)$ and write $A_{\vo}=(\vec{e_1},\cdots,\vec{e_r})$. By elementary divisor theorem, there are $\gamma,\gamma_{\idlJ} \in \SL_r(\ag{Z})$ and some $d_i \in \ag{Z}-\{0\}, d_i \mid d_{i+1}, 
orm[d_1 \cdots d_r] = 
orm[\vo/\idlJ] = 
orm[\idlJ^{-1} / \vo]$, such that $$ A_{\idlJ^{-1}}^{-1} = \gamma \diag(d_1,\cdots,d_r) \gamma_{\idlJ} A_{\vo}^{-1}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Write $A_{\idlJ^{-1}}^{-1} = \gamma \diag(d_i) \gamma_{\idlJ} A_{\vo}^{-1}$ with $|d_1\cdots d_r| = \norm[\vo/\idlJ]$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 5.35 to bound the operator norm and conclude part (1)
nodes.statement: Changing $\gamma$ is equivalent to changing the choice of basis $\alpha_i$ for $\idlJ^{-1}$. Applying Lemma \ref{CongGpLemma}, we can find $\gamma$ such that $$ \diag(d_1,\cdots,d_r)^{-1} \gamma \diag(d_1,\cdots,d_r) \gamma_{\idlJ} = N_+ N_- $$ where $N_+$ resp. $N_-$ is upper resp. lower unipotent with entries lying in $[-\frac{d_r}{2d_1}, \frac{d_r}{2d_1}]$. We thus get a bound of the operator norm $$ \Norm[A_{\idlJ^{-1}}^{-1}]_2 = \Norm[\diag(d_1,\cdots,d_r) N_+N_- A_{\vo}^{-1}]_2 \leq \norm[d_r] \left( r+\frac{r(r-1)d_r^2}{8d_1^2} \right) \Norm[A_{\vo}^{-1}]_2. $$ We finally estimate and conclude by \begin{align*} \sum_{\alpha \in \idlJ^{-1} - \{0\}} f_c(t\sigma(\alpha)) &= \sum_{\alpha \in \idlJ^{-1} - \{0\}} \Norm[t\sigma(\alpha)]_{\idlJ^{-1}}^{-c} \frac{\Norm[t\sigma(\alpha)]_{\idlJ^{-1}}^c}{\Norm[t\sigma(\alpha)]_2^c} f_c(t\sigma(\alpha)) \Norm[t\sigma(\alpha)]_2^c \\ &\leq t^{-c} \norm[d_r]^c \left( r+\frac{r(r-1)d_r^2}{8d_1^2} \right)^c \Norm[A_{\vo}^{-1}]_2^c (r_1+r_2)^{\frac{c}{2}} \sum_{\vec{n} \in \ag{Z}^r-\{0\}} \Norm[\vec{n}]_2^{-c}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Choosing $\gamma$ by the congruence lemma bounds $\Norm[A_{\idlJ^{-1}}^{-1}]_2$, giving the $t^{-c}\norm[\vo/\idlJ]^{3c}$ estimate.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.37
